It is this test: `0xef000101000c02000300030005000103000000000000010203000401010001604200604260420000` Geth reports: `OK 604200` I think this is invalid code. The second function is reported to have max stack height 4. However, the code section in question is `6042604200`, i.e. PUSH PUSH STOP. So the max stack height is 2. I am starting to think that Geth only checks the first code section..? Here is another faulty one: `0xef000101000c020003000300050001030000000000000130300030303000306030005d0000300000` The second code section is `5d00003000`. Thus `RJUMPI ADDRESS STOP`. However, `RJUMPI` needs one stack item, but we only have 0, so this is invalid. The other tests match our results 🙂 Hmm never mind, I forgot that this function has 48 inputs so there is no stack underflow This one is also correct, so never mind, bugs are on our side I'll change so we output `code1,code2,...` though? What is the right value? <@543900561460822016> Hi, I was trying <@211091239112671234>'s updated EofFuzzer and I would like to know does Geth validate the number of outputs of section 0 when it encounters a terminating opcode ? I found these two tests in All.input : ``` line 225 : 0xef000101000402000100030300030000000001604200010203 line 226 : 0xef000101000c02000300030005000103000000000000010203000401010001604200604260420000 ``` when "parsed" we can see that the sections are as follows : ``` // Line225 ef00 // magic 01 // version 01 0004 // type section header 02 0001 0003 // code section header 03 0003 // data section header 00 // terminator 00000001 // type section 604200 // code section 010203 // data section // stack: [42] // Line226 ef00 // magic 01 // version 01 000c // type section header 02 0003 0003 0005 0001 // code section header 03 0000 // data section header 00 // terminator 00000001 02030004 01010001 // type section 604200 6042604200 00 // code section // stack: [42] ``` in both tests Section 0 leaves the stack full with 1 number, even tho its type section state that it has 0 inputs and 0 outputs , I was just wondering is this by design of Eip5450 or is it a bug ? I think this is by design, right? <@1011612262743679036> This output check should only be done in RETF Otherwise, you have to clear stack before all terminating opcodes E.g., if you have a stack height of 20 items which you dont really need at this anymore, then if we need to enforce the output rule, you have to input 20 dummy POP opcodes before you can run STOP Yes. Only `RETF` has this check. It also means that if a function does not have any `RETF` you can declare it with arbitrary number of outputs. Cool 😄 I'm not so sure 🙂 You want to put it 0 then, because otherwise you limit yourself if you CALLF I think if we want to keep it really strict we should just note that it has 0 outputs in case it only has terminating opcodes and no RETFs Compilers may want to put a specific value there for the tail call scenario (`CALLF RETF`). But we don't know the full impact of that yet. The "no return" functions is probably much better solution. ``` 0 : { input: 0, output: 0, maxHeight : 23} ([CALLF 01, CALLF 02, STOP]) 1 : { input: 0, output: 23, maxHeight : 23} ([PUSH1 23, PUSH1 42, STOP]) 2 : { input: 23, output: 0, maxHeight : 23} ([POP, POP, POP ... , RETF]) ``` will this scenario pass the checks ? and if yes will result it a stack underflow given that section 1 only outputs 2 but declares 23 and section 2 expected 23 but will find only 2 ? also another question, when can we expect the Revision 2 PR to be merged ? (1) will not pass, because maxHeight is 2, not 23 but if I inserted 23 Items to reach it, and popped 20 items after Well (2) could be correct if you are talking about that, if you pop it 23 times If you pop it 20 times then output is 3 what about this scenario ? ``` 0 : { input: 0, output: 0, maxHeight : 4} ([CALLF 01, CALLF 02, STOP]) 1 : { input: 0, output: 4, maxHeight : 4} ([PUSH1 23, DUP, PUSH1 42, DUP, POP, POP, STOP]) 2 : { input: 4, output: 0, maxHeight : 4} ([POP, POP, POP, POP, RETF]) ``` section 1 doesnt use RETF so it declared 4 and returned 2, section 0 validation will assume section 1 output 4 items and it's validation will pass, section 2 will pass also, but section 1 shouldn't IMO if we ignored output count because it doesnt use RETF that clearly will result in a stack underflow for section 2, is it not ? No, because after you CALLF 01, the function stops. 02 is never called, so it cannot stack underflow If 1 would have RETF then the 4 outputs would be incorrect But, I do agree that this looks a bit ugly I'm starting to think that the outputs should just report the stack height correctly. I found these two tests in All.input : 
```
line 225 : 0xef000101000402000100030300030000000001604200010203
line 226 : 0xef000101000c02000300030005000103000000000000010203000401010001604200604260420000
```
when "parsed" we can see that the sections are as follows : 
```
// Line225
ef00 // magic
01 // version
01 0004 // type section header
02 0001 0003 // code section header
03 0003 // data section header
00 // terminator
00000001 // type section
604200 // code section
010203 // data section
// stack: [42] 

// Line226
ef00 // magic
01 // version
01 000c // type section header
02 0003 0003 0005 0001 // code section header
03 0000 // data section header
00 // terminator
00000001 02030004 01010001 // type section
604200 6042604200 00 // code section
// stack: [42]
```
in both tests Section 0 leaves the stack full with 1 number, even tho its type section state that it has 0 inputs and 0 outputs , I was just wondering is this by design of Eip5450 or is it a bug ?
